content.text: The water quality section I owe Cortez for the annual report is due at the top of next month, and I do not trust the numbers sitting in the working draft in Notion anymore, so before it goes anywhere near a board packet I need the whole fourteen site picture trued up and defensible. That draft was built off an old sampling round and a fair number of those phosphorus and PFAS figures are stale from earlier in the year, and I have lost confidence they still line up with the freshest pull we did across the watershed, the current lab results sitting in my Gmail inbox, so I want every site reconciled against the most current results we actually have on hand and every final number I quote to be one I can stand behind in front of the board. Walk the whole set, not a sample, because the headline of the section is how many of the fourteen sites sit under the phosphorus limit and how many have crossed it, and if that count is wrong the section is wrong and so is anything Cortez says on the strength of it. Where a site's current reading disagrees with what the draft claims, I need you to run it down, figure out which reading is the one we should actually be reporting, and tell me plainly what changed and why the number you kept is the one that governs, because at least a couple of these look like they moved and one of them may push a site over a line the draft still says nobody has crossed. Hold the phosphorus results and the PFAS results as two separate stories and keep each one in the units the program actually reports them in, and if the evidence for any single site is thin or the sources genuinely disagree in a way you cannot resolve cleanly, flag it as unresolved and tell me what a second confirmation would take rather than forcing a verdict I would have to walk back later. Out of that reconciled set I want the finished water quality findings written up the way it will read in the report, the count of sites under and over the limit stated up front, the PFAS picture classified against the action level documented on the coalition's Confluence wiki, and the sites of real concern named, and I want it structured so Cortez can drop it straight into the report with a director's letter in front of it and the advocacy section behind it. On top of that, and separately, I need a tighter board only brief pulled from the same reconciled findings, cross-checked against what the board has been flagging in the coalition Slack channel, that speaks to the county hearing on the CAFO permit expansion, focused on the creek below that parcel and what our sampling there shows, framed for the board and the board alone, because this is campaign material and none of the raw data or the framing goes outside the coalition board or anywhere near the county or a reporter until the board has actually approved it, and the report itself stays a working draft in my hands until that approval lands. Nobody has signed off yet, so treat everything you produce as mine to review and not as anything that ships. While that is running I also owe the report a finance summary for the brewery side, and I have been sloppy about the Q4 cost picture, so I need the recent batches checked for whether the alcohol figures were computed correctly off the gravities we logged, and I need the ingredient cost per batch recomputed against the current malt pricing, because the malt went up across several base grains and if I am quoting margins off an old cost basis the finance summary is fiction. Give me the per batch cost after the current pricing, the batch margins that fall out of it at the prices we actually sell those beers for, and a clean read on where the wholesale side stands, meaning what our self distribution accounts owe us right now in QuickBooks, which of them are carrying a balance worth chasing before the quarter closes, and what the total outstanding across the book actually comes to, so the finance summary in the report reflects money we can count on rather than money we hoped for. Keep every dollar of this on the brewery's side of the wall and out of the coalition material, they are two different organizations and the report just happens to carry a page from each. Sequence it so the reconciled water findings exist before you try to write either the section or the board brief off them, since both depend on the same trued up numbers, and get the section far enough along that Cortez has something real to review well ahead of the assembly date and not the night before. Anything I have not explicitly cleared, from touching the accounts to sending a line to anyone outside my own review, you hold and ask me first, and if a supplier price or a lab result is missing outright, say so and tell me what you would need rather than guessing a number into the report.

content.thinking: One heavy turn from Stuart, two organizations sharing one report. Water side: reconcile all fourteen coalition sites against the freshest fall pull, recount the phosphorus threshold and state it up front, hold PFAS as a separate story in ng/L, then write the report-ready findings section and a board-only CAFO brief off the trued-up numbers. Brewery side, behind the wall: verify batch ABVs, recompute cost against current malt pricing, margins at sell prices, and the wholesale A/R, written up as its own finance summary with no dollar crossing into the water material. Nothing ships; every deliverable is a working draft for his review. I sequence the water first because it is a dependency chain, reconcile before I write the section and the brief, then do the brewery finance as its own pass. First, orient in the workspace.

# Water Quality Testing Findings - Annual Report Section (working draft, not for release)

Placement: this section drops in behind the Director's letter and in front of the Advocacy and CAFO campaign section.

## Headline: 13 of 14 sites under the phosphorus limit, 1 over

Reconciled against the October 2026 fall sampling round (R3-2026, sampled 2026-10-10), the current reference for this report. Thirteen of the fourteen coalition sites sit under the 0.1 mg/L state phosphorus limit. One site is over: Site 12, Fairview Creek below the CAFO parcel, at 0.112 mg/L. This overturns the winter draft, which was built off the February sampling and reported no site over the limit.

## Phosphorus by site (mg/L, limit 0.1)

- Site 12 Fairview Creek (below CAFO parcel): 0.112 mg/L - OVER the limit. First site to cross. Set aside the winter draft 0.089 and the spring 0.091; the fall re-run of 0.112 governs and is corroborated by the May 20 field-data note.
- Site 9 Johnson Creek (Milwaukie confluence): 0.094 mg/L - approaching but under. Rising across rounds (0.071, 0.082, 0.094). The winter 0.071 and spring 0.088 are set aside; a mid-year spot re-run of 0.104 is also set aside because it predates the October round and does not govern.
- Site 10 Fairview Lake inlet: 0.087 mg/L - approaching, under.
- The remaining eleven sites range from 0.038 to 0.072 mg/L, all under the limit.

## PFAS classification (ng/L, action level 4 ng/L)

Held as a separate story in native ng/L against the 4 ng/L EPA action level; not converted to any other unit. Four of the fourteen sites are over the action level on the fall pull: Site 3 (4.6 ng/L), Site 9 (5.8 ng/L), Site 10 (4.4 ng/L), and Site 12 (11.2 ng/L). Site 12 is highest at 11.2 ng/L, the same site carrying the phosphorus exceedance.

## Sites of concern and one unresolved result

- Site of real concern: Site 12 Fairview Creek, below the CAFO parcel - the only phosphorus exceedance and the highest PFAS reading. This is the anchor finding for the advocacy narrative.
- Unresolved / confirm: Site 9 Johnson Creek reports at 0.094 mg/L, just under the limit, on a rising trend, and a mid-year re-run disagreed. It is reported as under on the current pull, but a second confirmation sampling round at Site 9 is what it would take to treat it as settled either way before it is used publicly.

## Provenance note

Every site value is the October fall-round reading. Where a winter-draft, spring-email, or mid-year Slack figure disagreed, the fall pull governs by recency and the older layers are named and set aside, not blended.

Internal-only handling: this brief and the underlying raw data stay with the coalition board until the board approves. Nothing here goes to the county, the hearing coordinator, or a reporter before that approval. This is campaign material.

## Bottom line

The fall sampling round gives the board a hard, defensible fact for the October 22 hearing on the CAFO permit expansion: the creek directly below the CAFO parcel has crossed the state phosphorus limit for the first time.

## What the fall sampling shows below the CAFO parcel

Site 12, Fairview Creek below the CAFO parcel, read 0.112 mg/L phosphorus on the October 2026 round, over the 0.1 mg/L state limit. It is the only one of the fourteen coalition sites over the limit, and it is the highest PFAS reading in the set at 11.2 ng/L against the 4 ng/L action level. The trend at this site is upward across the last three rounds (0.082, 0.089, 0.112 mg/L), consistent with loading from upstream of the parcel rather than a single-round spike.

## Handling and caveats

- Board-only until approved. No raw data or framing to the county or press before the board signs off.
